column1: # Translation glossary (Korean -> English) for the English version of this course. Read by book/check_translation.py.
# Columns (tab separated): ko[|ko ...] / English variants separated by | (the first one is the preferred translation) / flags / note.
# flags: count = the English text must use these terms at least as often as the Korean text does. A term with no flag only has to appear once.

# Matching: Korean terms match as substrings (a Korean term written as re:PATTERN is a regular expression, used when a plain substring gives false hits, e.g. 지지 inside 공정해지지). English variants of 4+ letters also match inflections (reproduc matches reproduction), shorter ones match exactly.
# Later rows override earlier rows with the same Korean term. The first block is taken from resources/glossary.md, the second block adds the vocabulary of the process documents.
# Style: American spelling, ISO dates, numbers and units unchanged. Keep the markers (green/yellow/red circles, warning sign, dagger, pencil, check marks) exactly as in the Korean text.
# Verdict words: 지지 -> supported, 지지되지 않음 -> not supported. A statement that the Korean text marks as unconfirmed must never become a confirmed one in English.
# 시험 실행 -> dry run. Gloss it at first use in each document: the author's own rehearsal of the workflow, not a pilot with learners.
# 대조 has no fixed row: use comparison, cross-check or check against depending on the sentence; 음성 대조 and 양성 대조 are negative control and positive control.
# 과제 is exercise in the module exercises files and task elsewhere.
